title: The harp (1 Samuel 16:14–23)
hookLine: young David plays, and the troubled king is refreshed

lines: FIND A MAN WHO CAN PLAY.
cards: Yesterday ended with the Spirit of the LORD coming upon David. The very next verse: "But the Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD troubled him." One young man filled.
One king emptied, and tormented. Nothing says Saul's servants know about the oil in Bethlehem. What they can see is that their king is not well.
Find a man who can play the harp, they say, and when the trouble comes on you, he'll play with his hand, "and thou shalt be well."

teach.h: AN EVIL SPIRIT FROM THE LORD.
teach.b: Start with the hard phrase: an evil spirit from the LORD. Readers have wrestled with it. Some understand it as a real spiritual being that God permits to trouble Saul.
Others read it as the text's way of saying that Saul's own darkness, his fear and his rage, became a kind of judgment.
Some modern readers hear something like deep anguish or depression, though the text doesn't use our words, and gives no diagnosis. Whatever it is, it comes in waves, and it hurts.

teach.h: CUNNING IN PLAYING, AND THE LORD WITH HIM.
teach.b: Then one servant names a name: "I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite, that is cunning in playing." Brave, he adds, a man of war, prudent, comely, and the LORD is with him.
So Saul sends to Jesse: "Send me David thy son, which is with the sheep."

The anointed boy walks into the court of the king he'll replace, with a donkey laden with bread, a bottle of wine and a young goat from his father. The text says Saul loves him greatly and makes him his armor bearer.
Nothing in the text says Saul knows who he's hired. The Hebrew word for the instrument is kinnor, a stringed instrument; the King James says harp, and some modern translations say lyre.

Then the chapter's last verse: "when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took an harp, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him." Refreshed.
No speech, no fix for what was wrong. Just a boy, a few strings, and a tormented man able to breathe again, for now.

how: Christians sing and play music as part of worship, and some point to David playing for Saul when they talk about music as comfort for the troubled.

games.q: music in Saul's court — tap the pairs.
p: what Saul was when David played

s: Saul took a dislike to David as soon as he arrived
Saul loved him greatly, and David became his armor bearer (1 Samuel 16:21).
David came to Saul's court empty-handed
Jesse sent him with an ass laden with bread, a bottle of wine and a kid (1 Samuel 16:20).
when David played, Saul was refreshed, and was well
1 Samuel 16:23, the last verse of the chapter.

games.q: you're one of Saul's servants. the king is tormented, and nothing calms him. what do you suggest?
o: send for a warrior to guard him.
find a man who can play the harp.
leave him alone until it passes.
games.why: they seek a cunning player on an harp (16:16), and the one they find is the boy Samuel has just anointed.

practice: If you can, put on one quiet piece of music, play something yourself, or hum; if you can't, listen to the quietest sounds around you as if they were music. If you pray, the Psalms are there to borrow.
Music can help, but when the trouble is heavy it isn't the only help, and reaching for a person is part of the cure too.

wordCard.voice: The harp. David's kinnor in Saul's court. When the trouble came on the king, David played with his hand, and Saul was refreshed, and was well.

carryVoice: Your line: music can heal. Saul was refreshed, and was well, for a time. See you tomorrow.
